draft.emotion: reflective and slightly nostalgic, looking back at something from a distance
notes: Before a noun, 'viejo' expresses long-standing history or affection ('un viejo amigo', an old friend); after a noun, it states literal age ('un amigo viejo', an elderly friend).

Calling a person 'viejo' can sound blunt; 'mayor' (older) or 'grande' (in Mexico) is more polite. As a noun ('el viejo' / 'la vieja'), it is also common Mexican slang for husband/wife or father/mother.

senses.definition: Of a person, animal, or thing: having lived or existed for a long time.

examples.text: Mi abuelo es un hombre muy viejo pero muy sabio.
examples.translation: My grandfather is a very old man, but very wise.
examples.emotion: tender and respectful, speaking of someone with great life experience

senses.definition: Of an object: having been used for a long time and no longer new.

examples.text: Compré un carro viejo para aprender a manejar.
examples.translation: I bought an old car to learn how to drive.

senses.definition: Used before a noun: known for a long time, or from an earlier time.

examples.text: Ayer me encontré a un viejo amigo de la escuela.
examples.translation: Yesterday I ran into an old friend from school.
